Public Utility Commission of Texas                                                IREN Limited
1701 N. Congress Avenue, 7th Floor                                                Level 6, 55 Market Street
                                                                                  Sydney, NSW 2000
Austin, TX 78701


Dear PUCT Commissioners,


      IREN Comments on PUCT Project No. 58481 – Rulemaking to Implement Large Load
                    Interconnection Standards Under PURA §37.0561


IREN appreciates Staff and the Commissions’ work in putting together the initial proposal for
publication and for allowing stakeholders the ability to provide comments and suggested revisions.

IREN Limited and its affiliates (“IREN”) are in the business of building and operating next-generation
data centers across Canada, United States and Asia-Pacific, powered by 100% renewable energy.
As of February 2026, IREN owns and operates 650MW of operating data centers in ERCOT and an
additional 2,000MW of financially committed data center capacity in ERCOT, secured by executed
interconnection agreements and under construction. IREN’s wholly owned subsidiary, IE US
Development Holdings 3 Inc., is an ERCOT member.

Given the importance of the large load interconnection process, we are hereby providing comments
to the Commission’s Proposal for Publication in Project No. 58481.

Intermediate Agreement
    1. Standard agreement: We recommend that a standardized intermediate agreement
       template is developed to improve the efficiency and transparency of the documentation
       process for large load interconnections and result in standardization among utilities.
    2. Site control: Binding options to lease or purchase should be considered suitable forms of
       site control at this early stage of a development, before studies have been
       conducted/concluded.
    3. Site studies and regulatory approvals: We recommend this be removed from the
       intermediate agreement phase given the early stage of development.
    4. Financial security: We are supportive of meaningful financial security being posted to
       reduce the impact of speculative loads on the study process noting $100,000 per MW at
       such an early stage of development may stifle economic development in Texas. We
       recommend a lower threshold of $50,000 per MW.

Interconnection Agreement
    1. Standard agreement: Similar to our comment above, we recommend a standardized
        interconnection agreement to streamline the connection process and to ensure
        standardization amongst utilities.
    2. Site control: We agree that requiring an executed lease or deed of sale should be required
        at this stage of the connection process, however, recommend that the minimum lease term
        should be 20 years, not 5 years, as this more closely reflects the minimum expected life of a
        large load project
    3. Site studies and regulatory approvals: We agree that providing this information is suitable
        at this stage of the interconnection process. We recommend that a standard list of studies
        and approvals be developed which the customer can respond to, as this will increase the
        efficiency and transparency of the process.
    4. Non-refundable interconnection fee: We are supportive of this concept. Similar to our
        comment above on financial security, we recommend a lower threshold of $50,000 per
        MW.




                                                                                                     1
 Refunds and non-utilized capacity

    1. Non-utilized capacity: We agree a key pillar of this rule should be allocating or reallocating
       capacity to real and viable projects and not allowing developers to ‘sit’ on capacity for an
       indefinite period of time. Construction schedule changes can occur with the scale and
       complexity of large load projects. Given this, we recommend the requirement to notify
       ERCOT of non-utilized capacity is extended from 6 to 12 months. We also recommend that
       the PUCT and/or ERCOT clearly define a failed milestone, for example, should this be tied to
       installed project capacity, actual peak demand or another metric.


We appreciate your time and consideration in reviewing our comments.



Sincerely,




Lindsay Ward                                                       Jason Date
Senior Advisor (formerly President)                                Associate Director Development
